cards.text: Jeremiah, the LORD's prophet, tells this one himself. The LORD says to him, "Go down at once to the potter's house, and there I will give you My message." Go now, hear why later, and friend, I'd have had SO many questions on the walk down.

cards.question: Jeremiah walks into the potter's house. What's the potter doing when he gets there?

cards.text: The potter's shaping a vessel from the clay, wheel spinning. Then, right there in his hand, the vessel becomes flawed.

cards.question: The vessel the potter is shaping becomes flawed in his hand. What does he do with the clay?

cards.text: He reshapes it however seems best to him. Baker, I KNOW this move: lopsided cookie, roll it back up, stamp it again, and nobody ever has to know.

cards.question: Then the word of the LORD comes to Jeremiah, for the house of Israel. The LORD asks if He can treat them the way this potter treats his clay.

cards.text: Then the LORD lays out how it works. At any time, He might announce that a nation or kingdom will be uprooted, torn down and destroyed.

cards.question: If the nation the LORD warned turns from its evil, He says the disaster comes anyway.

cards.text: Now flip it around. Say the LORD announces He will build up and establish a nation or kingdom.

cards.question: Say the LORD announces He will build up a nation, but it does evil in His sight and doesn't listen to His voice. What does He say about the good He intended for it?

answers.text: He will pass it to another

cards.text: Now it hits home. The LORD has Jeremiah tell the men of Judah and the residents of Jerusalem that He is planning a disaster for them.

cards.question: Right after telling Judah and Jerusalem about that disaster, what does the LORD tell each of them to do?
The LORD tells Jeremiah that the people of Judah will answer His call to turn by promising to turn from their evil ways.

cards.text: Instead, the LORD says they'll call it hopeless and follow their own plans, each acting on the stubbornness of his evil heart. Friend, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer sure my story was over, and even I wasn't that committed to it.
Then the LORD says to inquire among the nations: who has ever heard things like these? He says, "Virgin Israel has done a most terrible thing."
He asks if the snow of Lebanon ever leaves its rocky slopes, or if its cool waters ever run dry.

cards.question: Lebanon's snow stays put and its waters keep flowing. But the LORD says His people have ___ Him.

cards.text: They burn incense to worthless idols. And those idols make them stumble in their ways.

cards.question: The LORD describes the road His people have picked. Where are they walking?

answers.text: On rutted bypaths off the highway
On the ancient roads of old

cards.text: They leave the ancient roads for the bumpy back way. Friend, that's ditching the highway because your phone found a shortcut, and forty potholes later you are STILL not there.

cards.question: The LORD says that all who pass by the land His people have made a desolation will be appalled and shake their heads.
The LORD says He'll scatter His people before the enemy like the east wind. In the day of their calamity, what will He show them?

answers.text: His back and not His face

cards.text: Then some people start making plans. That word again, and this time the plans are against Jeremiah.

cards.question: The people plotting against Jeremiah say the priest will still have the law, the wise will still have counsel and the prophet will still have an oracle. So what do they decide to do about Jeremiah?

answers.text: Denounce him and ignore his words
Bring his words to the king
Write his words on a scroll

cards.text: Now Jeremiah turns to the LORD. He says, "Attend to me, O LORD. Hear what my accusers are saying!"

cards.question: With his accusers coming after him, Jeremiah asks the LORD: should good be repaid with ___?

cards.text: Yet they've dug a pit for him. I think that one stings.

cards.question: Speaking to the LORD, Jeremiah reminds Him what he did for his accusers. What was it?

cards.text: Then Jeremiah says some hard words. He asks the LORD to hand their children over to famine, pour out the power of the sword on them, and let a cry be heard from their houses when He suddenly brings raiders against them.

cards.question: Jeremiah says that besides digging a pit to capture him, they've hidden snares for his feet.
Jeremiah asks the LORD to wipe out the guilt of the people plotting against him.

cards.text: Instead, he says the LORD knows all their deadly plots against him, and he asks the LORD to let them be overthrown and to deal with them in the time of His anger. I think that's about as honest as anyone gets with God, friend.
